annotations.title: Mathlib 4.26.0 Breaking Change: IsStoppingTime API
annotations.body: During formalization, we discovered that Mathlib 4.26.0 changed `IsStoppingTime` from `τ : Ω → ι` to `τ : Ω → WithTop ι`. This means FairGamesTheorem.lean (written for an older API) has pre-existing build failures. The `stoppedValue` function now uses `WithTop.untopA` for evaluation. Four theorems in this file remain as sorries pending resolution of the `stoppedValue`/`untopA` simp API.
annotations.mathContext: `WithTop ℕ` (also written `ℕ∞`) is `ℕ ⊕ {⊤}` — the extended naturals with a top element `⊤ = ∞` representing "never stop". `IsStoppingTime ℱ (τ : Ω → ℕ∞)` means `∀ n : ℕ, {ω | τ ω ≤ ↑n} ∈ ℱ n`, where `↑n : ℕ∞` is the coercion. The old API `τ : Ω → ℕ` forced stopping to be finite, making `⊤` impossible to represent. `stoppedValue f τ ω` is now defined as `f (WithTop.untopD 0 (τ ω)) ω` — `untopD d x` extracts the ℕ value from `ℕ∞` with default `d` when `x = ⊤`. The four sorry'd theorems fail because unfolding `stoppedValue` produces `WithTop.untopD 0 (τ ω)` goals that require specific `simp` lemmas about `untopD`/`untopA` commutativity with arithmetic that weren't stabilized in Mathlib 4.26.0. The martingale time-invariance proof sidesteps this entirely by using `setIntegral_eq` instead of `stoppedValue`.

annotations.title: Martingale Time Invariance via setIntegral_eq
annotations.body: **Core insight**: E[f_n] = E[f_0] is proved using `Martingale.setIntegral_eq` with `s = Set.univ`, rather than the Optional Stopping Theorem directly. This bypasses the `τ : Ω → ℕ∞` API complexity. The proof is: `hf.setIntegral_eq (Nat.zero_le n) MeasurableSet.univ`, then `simp only [Measure.restrict_univ]`.
annotations.mathContext: `Martingale.setIntegral_eq` has signature: `hf.setIntegral_eq (h : i ≤ j) (hs : MeasurableSet s) : ∫ ω in s, f i ω ∂μ = ∫ ω in s, f j ω ∂μ`. The full integral over `Set.univ` is a set-restricted integral with `s = Set.univ`. After `hf.setIntegral_eq (Nat.zero_le n) MeasurableSet.univ`, we get `h : ∫ ω in Set.univ, f 0 ω ∂μ = ∫ ω in Set.univ, f n ω ∂μ`. Then `simp only [Measure.restrict_univ] at h` rewrites `μ.restrict Set.univ` to `μ` (since restricting to the whole space is the identity), giving `h : ∫ ω, f 0 ω ∂μ = ∫ ω, f n ω ∂μ`. Finally `exact h.symm` reverses the equality. The instance `[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]` is needed because `Martingale.setIntegral_eq` requires `SigmaFiniteFiltration ℱ μ`, which follows from `IsFiniteMeasure` (subsumed by `IsProbabilityMeasure`). An alternative proof path: define constant stopping time `τ(ω) = n` (always stops at step $n$), verify it's a valid `ℕ∞`-stopping time, apply Optional Stopping; but this requires the `stoppedValue` API that's blocked by the 4.26.0 change.
prerequisites: Filtration and Adapted processes in Lean 4

annotations.title: Gambler's Ruin Formula (Algebraic)
annotations.body: The key step: from `p * (W₀ + a) = W₀` (the fair game condition), we derive `p = W₀/(W₀+a)` by dividing both sides by `W₀ + a`. This requires only `rw [eq_div_iff hWa]; linarith` — the Optional Stopping Theorem has already done the hard work by establishing E[final wealth] = E[initial wealth].
annotations.mathContext: `eq_div_iff hWa : b / c = a ↔ b = a * c` (when `c ≠ 0`). `rw [eq_div_iff hWa]` transforms the goal `p = W₀ / (W₀ + a)` to `p * (W₀ + a) = W₀`, which is exactly `hfair`. Then `linarith` closes it. `hWa : W₀ + a ≠ 0` is proved by `ne_of_gt (by linarith)` using `hW : 0 < W₀` and `ha : 0 < a`. The complementary result `gamblers_ruin_lose_prob` chains through: `hp_eq : p = W₀/(W₀+a)` from the first theorem, then `rw [hp_eq]`, `field_simp [hWa]`, `ring` simplifies `1 - W₀/(W₀+a) = a/(W₀+a)` after clearing denominators. The third theorem `gamblers_ruin_probs_sum_one` is just `by ring` since `p + (1 - p) = 1` is algebraic identity. The stochastic content (that a fair game satisfies `p * (W₀ + a) + (1-p) * 0 = W₀`) is imported as hypothesis `hfair`; these theorems only prove the algebraic implication. In classical Gambler's Ruin: player starts at $W_0 \in \{1, \ldots, N-1\}$, wins or loses £1 per step with equal probability, stops at 0 (ruin) or $N = W_0 + a$ (goal). Ruin probability = $a/N$, success = $W_0/N$.

annotations.title: Axiom Elimination via Mathlib iff
annotations.body: The axiom `submartingale_of_stoppedValue_mono` in FairGamesTheorem.lean is the backward direction of Mathlib's `submartingale_iff_expected_stoppedValue_mono`. This theorem eliminates it: `rw [submartingale_iff_expected_stoppedValue_mono hadapt hint]` rewrites the Submartingale goal to the iff's RHS, then `exact h` closes the goal in one step. The hypothesis `h` is stated with ℕ∞ stopping times (the Mathlib 4.26.0 API), unlike the axiom which used ℕ.
annotations.mathContext: `submartingale_iff_expected_stoppedValue_mono hadapt hint` has type `Submartingale f ℱ μ ↔ ∀ τ π : Ω → ℕ∞, IsStoppingTime ℱ τ → IsStoppingTime ℱ π → τ ≤ π → (∃ N, ∀ ω, π ω ≤ N) → ∫ ω, stoppedValue f τ ω ∂μ ≤ ∫ ω, stoppedValue f π ω ∂μ`. When the goal is `Submartingale f ℱ μ`, `rw [submartingale_iff_expected_stoppedValue_mono hadapt hint]` uses the iff to rewrite the goal to the RHS — this is Lean 4's `rw` applied to a proposition at the goal position (not a `simp` lemma). The new goal is exactly the type of `h`, so `exact h` closes it. In type-theoretic terms: `Iff.mpr : (P ↔ Q) → Q → P`; the `rw` converts `P` goal to `Q`, then `exact h : Q` closes it — effectively this is `exact (submartingale_iff_expected_stoppedValue_mono hadapt hint).mpr h`. The two arguments `hadapt : Adapted ℱ f` and `hint : ∀ n, Integrable (f n) μ` are needed because the iff requires these as hypotheses for the backward direction. By proving this as a theorem in `FairGamesOQ03` rather than an `axiom` in `FairGamesTheorem`, the logical strength of the overall development decreases by 1 assumption.
